title: A Torsion-Free Group Algebra That Is Not Directly Finite

issues.description: Not an error, a caution. The claim implies a non-sofic group exists (via Elek–Szabó), which is a major open problem. Correctness depends entirely on the probabilistic exclusion of spherical arrangements. That step runs with very small margins: lambda≈0.9939, so delta≈0.0015 and epsilon≈1.6e-5. It also relies on a slowly vanishing bound, exp(-delta L/(4M)+o(L)) with L≈c0 log n. Every step I checked is valid, but the o(L) uniformity claims (pattern entropy, grid alignment, kappa_L) are only sketched and deserve an expert's line-by-line check.

I did not consult the companion paper OpenAI2026ZD. This paper says it reproduces the needed arguments itself, and as far as I can tell it does.
main_claim: There is a finitely presented torsion-free group G with a finite 2-dimensional classifying complex, and a,b,c in F_2[G], such that ab=1, ac=0 and c≠0, so ba≠1. This is a counterexample to Kaplansky's direct finiteness conjecture over F_2, and it implies G is non-sofic. G is built as the fundamental group of a rose with cones attached on two random immersed labeled graphs. Their vertex label sets come from projective-plane lines plus Fano-complement extra letters, which force the parity conditions.
